_about: One-line explanations of everything EasyScript scripts can use. Shown by the code editor (hover and autocomplete) and the Scripting Reference. Keys: global names, self.<property or action>, list./text./dict./vec.<method>, event names and keywords.
abs: The number without its minus sign: abs(-3) is 3.
acos: The angle (in degrees) whose cosine is x.
asin: The angle (in degrees) whose sine is x.
atan: The angle (in degrees) whose tangent is x.
atan2: The angle (in degrees) of the direction (x, y). Handy for aiming: atan2(dy, dx).
bool: True or False: zero, empty text, empty lists and None count as False.
ceil: Rounds up to a whole number: ceil(2.1) is 3.
clamp: Keeps a value between low and high: clamp(15, 0, 10) is 10.
cos: The cosine of an angle in degrees (0 to 360, not radians).
dict: Makes an empty dictionary (a set of names and values), like {}.
exp: e to the power of x.
float: Turns text like "3.5" into a number.
floor: Rounds down to a whole number: floor(2.9) is 2.
game: Values every script shares, and that stay when the scene changes: game.score += 1.
get_game: Reads a game value, or gives the default if it hasn't been set yet: get_game("score", 0).
int: Turns a number or text into a whole number, dropping any decimals: int("7") is 7.
len: How many items are in a list or dictionary, or how many letters are in text.
lerp: Blends from a to b: t = 0 gives a, t = 1 gives b, t = 0.5 is halfway. Works with numbers, vectors and colors.
list: Makes a list from something you can loop over, or an empty list.
log: The natural logarithm of a number above 0.
max: The biggest of the values, or of the items in a list.
min: The smallest of the values, or of the items in a list.
move_toward: Moves a number toward a target by at most step, without going past it.
pow: x to the power of power: pow(2, 3) is 8. The same as x ** power.
print: Shows values in the Console. Great for checking what your code is doing.
range: Counts numbers for a loop: range(5) gives 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
reversed: A copy of a list in the opposite order.
round: Rounds to the nearest whole number, or to a number of decimal places: round(3.14159, 2) is 3.14.
sign: 1 for positive numbers, -1 for negative ones, 0 for zero.
sin: The sine of an angle in degrees. sin(time() * 90) goes smoothly up and down.
sorted: A sorted copy of a list. key= picks what to sort by, reverse=True sorts from biggest.
sqrt: The square root of a number.
str: Turns any value into text: str(42) is "42".
sum: Adds up all the numbers in a list.
tan: The tangent of an angle in degrees.
type: The kind of a value as text: "number", "text", "list", "dict", "vec", "color", "bool", "none", "function" or "object".
after: Calls a function once, after some seconds: after(2, explode). Gives back a timer you can stop.
delta_time: Seconds since the last frame (the same as dt in on_update).
every: Calls a function again and again, every so many seconds: every(1, spawn_enemy). Gives back a timer.
set_time_scale: Speeds the game up or slows it down: 0.5 is slow motion, 1 is normal, 0 freezes time.
start_task: Runs a function side by side with the rest of your code, so it can use wait() without holding anything up.
stop_timer: Stops a timer made by after() or every().
wait: Pauses this function for some seconds, then carries on. Works inside events like on_start().
axis: -1 to 1 from the arrow keys, WASD or a gamepad stick: axis("horizontal") or axis("vertical"). Also "look_x" and "look_y" for the right stick.
key_down: True while a key (or input action like "jump") is held down.
key_pressed: True only on the frame a key is pressed. Use it for jumping or shooting once per press.
key_released: True only on the frame a key is let go.
mouse_delta: How far the mouse moved since the last frame, in pixels.
mouse_down: True while a mouse button is held: "left", "right" or "middle".
mouse_position: Where the mouse points in the game world, as vec(x, y).
mouse_pressed: True only on the frame a mouse button is pressed.
mouse_released: True only on the frame a mouse button is let go.
mouse_screen_position: Where the mouse is on the screen, in pixels.
mouse_scroll: How much the mouse wheel turned this frame.
mouse_x: The x of the point the mouse is over in the game world.
mouse_y: The y of the point the mouse is over in the game world.
broadcast: Sends a message to every script: each one's on_message(message, data) runs.
camera: The main camera object, so you can move or change it.
camera_shake: Shakes the camera, e.g. for hits and explosions.
choice: A random item from a list.
random: A random number from 0 up to (not including) 1.
random_int: A random whole number from low to high, both included: random_int(1, 6) rolls a die.
random_range: A random number (with decimals) between low and high.
random_seed: Makes the random numbers come out the same every time the game runs.
shuffle: Mixes up the order of a list.
color: A color from a name ("red", "sky", "gold"...) or a code like "#ff8800".
hsv: A color from hue (0-360 around the color wheel), saturation and brightness (0-1).
rgb: A color from red, green and blue amounts, each 0 to 255. An optional 4th value (0-1) is how see-through it is.
vec: A 2D or 3D vector (a position, direction or size): vec(1, 2) or vec(1, 2, 3).
count: How many active objects have this tag.
create_sprite: Makes a new object with a shape ("circle", "star"...) or picture file, at x, y.
create_text: Makes a new text object at x, y.
destroy: Removes an object from the game.
find: The first object with this name, or None if there isn't one.
find_all: A list of every active object with this tag.
spawn: Makes a copy of a prefab at x, y and gives it back.
has_data: True if a value has been saved under this name.
load_data: Reads a value saved with save_data, or the default if nothing was saved.
save_data: Saves a value on the player's computer. It's still there the next time the game starts.
direction: The direction from one thing to another, as a vector of length 1.
distance: How far apart two objects or positions are.
is_fullscreen: True if the game fills the whole screen.
lock_mouse: Hides the mouse and keeps it in the game (for first-person games). lock_mouse(False) frees it.
screen_height: The height of the game view in pixels.
screen_width: The width of the game view in pixels.
set_fullscreen: Switches between fullscreen and a window.
is_paused: True while the game is paused.
load_scene: Goes to another scene: load_scene("level2") or load_scene("scenes/level2.scene").
pause_game: Stops game time: things stop moving, but scripts and buttons still work (for pause menus).
restart_scene: Starts the current scene again from the beginning.
play_music: Plays music on a loop. It keeps playing when the scene changes.
set_volume: The volume of every sound and the music, from 0 (silent) to 1.
raycast: Finds the first thing on a line from one point to another. Gives a dictionary with object, point, normal and distance, or None.
set_gravity: Changes gravity: set_gravity(0, -20) for 2D, or three values for 3D.
tween: Smoothly animates a number property of an object to a target over some seconds.
self: The object this script is on.
self.name: The object's name, as shown in the Hierarchy.
self.tag: A label for finding groups of objects, like "enemy" or "coin".
self.active: False turns the object off: it disappears and its scripts stop.
self.visible: False hides the object, but its scripts keep running.
self.id: A unique id for this object, as text.
self.exists: False once the object has been destroyed.
self.position: The position as a vector: vec(x, y) in 2D, vec(x, y, z) in 3D.
self.world_x: x in the world, even when the object is inside another one.
self.world_y: y in the world, even when the object is inside another one.
self.world_z: z in the world, even when the object is inside another one.
self.world_position: The position in the world, even when the object is inside another one.
self.angle: How far the object is turned, in degrees (around z in 2D, around y in 3D).
self.rotation: The rotation on every axis in degrees, as vec(x, y, z).
self.rotation_x: Rotation around the x axis, in degrees.
self.rotation_y: Rotation around the y axis, in degrees.
self.rotation_z: Rotation around the z axis, in degrees.
self.scale: How big the object is: 1 is normal, 2 is twice as big. Set a number or a vector.
self.size: The size of a sprite or UI element, as vec(width, height).
self.width: The width of a sprite or UI element.
self.height: The height of a sprite or UI element.
self.color: The object's color: color("red") or rgb(255, 0, 0).
self.alpha: How see-through the object is: 1 is solid, 0 is invisible.
self.text: The words shown by a text, UI text or button.
self.image: The picture file a sprite shows, like "images/hero.png".
self.frame: Which picture of a sprite sheet is shown.
self.flip_x: True mirrors the sprite left to right (to face the other way).
self.flip_y: True flips the sprite upside down.
self.order: Drawing order: sprites with a higher order are drawn on top.
self.velocity: Speed and direction per second. Needs a RigidBody2D, RigidBody or CharacterController.
self.velocity_x: Speed left and right, per second.
self.velocity_y: Speed up and down, per second.
self.parent: The object this one is inside, or None. Set it to move the object into another.
self.children: A list of the objects directly inside this one.
self.right: The direction to the object's right.
self.is_clone: True in copies made with self.clone().
self.destroy: Removes this object from the game.
self.damage: Takes health away (with the Health behavior). Without Health, the level starts again.
self.heal: Gives health back, up to the maximum (with the Health behavior).
self.move: Moves the object by an amount: self.move(2, 0) moves it 2 to the right.
self.move_forward: Moves the object in the direction it faces.
self.turn: Turns the object by some degrees.
self.look_at: Turns the object to face another object or a position.
self.move_toward: Moves toward a target by at most step. Gives True once it's there.
self.distance_to: How far this object is from another object or a position.
self.direction_to: The direction from this object to a target, as a vector of length 1.
self.is_touching: True if this object touches another object, or anything with a tag.
self.apply_force: Pushes a physics object a little, like wind. Use it every frame for a steady push.
self.apply_impulse: Kicks a physics object all at once, like a hit or a jump.
self.play_animation: Plays frames of a sprite sheet: self.play_animation(0, 3) plays frames 0 to 3.
self.stop_animation: Stops the sprite animation on the current frame.
self.tween: Smoothly animates a number property: self.tween("y", 5, 1) moves y to 5 over 1 second.
self.clone: Makes a copy of this object (the copy's is_clone is True) and gives it back.
self.hide: Hides the object (its scripts keep running).
self.get_component: A component of this object, so you can read and change its settings. None if it doesn't have one.
self.add_component: Adds a component, like "RigidBody2D", and gives it back.
self.has_component: True if the object has a component with this name.
self.remove_component: Removes a component from the object.
self.find_child: The object with this name somewhere inside this one, or None.
self.play_sound: Plays a sound once (the same as play_sound).
self.send: Calls a function in this object's script: other.send("hurt", 1) runs its hurt(1).
self.say: Shows a speech bubble above the object for a few seconds.
self.emit: Bursts out some particles (needs a ParticleEmitter).
self.set_tile: Puts a tile in a Tilemap at a column and row. Tile -1 erases.
self.get_tile: Which tile is at a column and row of a Tilemap, or -1 if it's empty.
self.set_tile_at: Puts a tile in a Tilemap at a world position. Tile -1 erases.
self.get_tile_at: Which tile is at a world position, or -1 if it's empty.
on_start: Runs once, when the object starts.
on_update: Runs every frame. dt is the seconds since the last frame: multiply speeds by it.
on_fixed_update: Runs 60 times a second, in step with physics.
on_collide: Runs when this object bumps into another one. other is the object it hit.
on_collide_end: Runs when this object stops touching another one.
on_trigger: Runs when something enters this trigger (a collider with Is Trigger ticked).
on_trigger_exit: Runs when something leaves this trigger.
on_click: Runs when the player clicks or taps this object or button.
on_key_pressed: Runs when any key is pressed. key is its name, like "space".
on_message: Runs when any script broadcasts a message.
on_destroy: Runs just before the object is removed.
list.append: Adds an item to the end of the list.
list.add: Adds an item to the end of the list (the same as append).
list.insert: Puts an item at a position in the list.
list.pop: Takes the last item (or the one at a position) out of the list and gives it back.
list.remove: Takes the first matching item out of the list.
list.index: The position of an item in the list, or -1 if it isn't there.
list.count: How many times an item is in the list.
list.extend: Adds all the items of another list.
list.copy: A separate copy of the list.
list.sort: Sorts the list. key= picks what to sort by, reverse=True sorts from biggest.
text.strip: The text without spaces at the start and end.
text.split: Cuts text into a list of words, or at a separator: "a,b".split(",").
text.join: Joins a list into one text, with this text in between: ", ".join(names).
text.replace: The text with every old part changed to new.
text.startswith: True if the text starts with this.
text.endswith: True if the text ends with this.
text.find: Where a part is in the text, or -1 if it isn't there.
text.count: How many times a part is in the text.
text.isdigit: True if the text is only digits.
text.capitalize: The text with its first letter capital.
text.title: The Text With Every Word Capital.
text.zfill: Pads the text with zeros in front: "7".zfill(3) is "007".
dict.keys: A list of the names in the dictionary.
dict.values: A list of the values in the dictionary.
dict.items: A list of [name, value] pairs, for looping over both.
dict.get: The value for a name, or a default if it isn't there.
dict.pop: Takes a name and its value out and gives the value back.
dict.copy: A separate copy of the dictionary.
dict.update: Adds (or replaces) every name and value from another dictionary.
vec.dot: The dot product with another vector: how much two directions point the same way.
vec.distance_to: How far this point is from another one.
vec.r: The red part of a color (0-1).
vec.g: The green part of a color (0-1).
vec.b: The blue part of a color (0-1).
def: Makes a function: def jump(): ... Events like on_start are functions Aven calls for you.
if: Runs the lines below only when something is True.
elif: Another check, tried when the ones above were False.
else: Runs when none of the checks above were True.
for: Repeats the lines below for each item: for enemy in find_all("enemy"):
in: Loops over items, or checks if something is in a list or text.
while: Repeats the lines below as long as something is True. Add wait() inside if it runs for a while.
return: Ends the function, and gives back a value if you write one.
continue: Skips to the next turn of the loop.
pass: Does nothing. A placeholder for code you'll write later.
and: True when both sides are True.
or: True when either side is True.
not: Turns True into False and False into True.
global: Lets a function change a variable from the top of the script (usually not needed in EasyScript).
